question: Which of the following enzymes can be considered a good marker of drug-induced hemolytic anemia ?:
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Drug-induced hemolytic anemia" -> "red blood cell destruction" -> "increased lactate dehydrogenase release" -> "elevated lactate dehydrogenase levels" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Drug-induced hemolytic anemia" -> "red blood cell destruction" -> "increased aspartate aminotransferase release" -> "elevated aspartate aminotransferase levels" -> 70%
CHAIN: "Drug-induced hemolytic anemia" -> "muscle damage unlikely" -> "creatine kinase not elevated" -> 20%
CHAIN: "Drug-induced hemolytic anemia" -> "G6PD deficiency possible cause" -> "G6PDH levels not directly elevated" -> 30%
analysis: Drug-induced hemolytic anemia is often associated with the deficiency of Glucose-6 phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PDH). This enzyme is crucial for the proper functioning of red blood cells, and its deficiency can lead to hemolysis when exposed to certain drugs. Therefore, G6PDH is a good marker for drug-induced hemolytic anemia.
